name: Kessav Yuzu-White Pepper Stim Drops
description: Small, translucent amber drops containing a standard-dose synth-caffeine-adenosine complex alongside yuzu citrus and cracked white pepper flavoring. Kessav's stim line is regulated under M88 food-pharma hybrid codes — each drop is individually stamped with a dose indicator.
flavor_profile: Bright yuzu citrus with a slow-building white pepper heat that amplifies the stimulant effect perceptually — clean and sharp
price: Φ5.50 for a tube of 10 drops
cultural_context: Standard issue in M88's gig-labor ecosystem — delivery riders, shift workers, and freelance fixers keep a tube in their kit. The white pepper heat has become associated with the feeling of waking up fast, and some users deliberately let the heat build before starting a task as a mental ritual.
story_hooks: A new black-market variant of Kessav Yuzu-White Pepper drops is circulating on the Shelf with triple the stimulant dose — and no safety stamp — leading to cardiac events in augmented users whose chrome can't compensate.
Kessav's licensed stimulant formula is up for regulatory review, and a rival Corponation is funding the opposition research hoping to get the product pulled so they can fill the market gap.

A Tier 3 office worker has been eating twice the recommended dose daily for eight months and is experiencing unusual synesthetic responses — tasting colors, hearing flavors — that her neurologist can't fully explain.
